Full admission overflow formula, capacity values and bandwidth unit conversions.
Implementations of helpers that search, move, enqueue or dequeue tasks and entities across queues.

findings.text: Server idle accounting, server start, bandwidth attach, bandwidth swap, and common execution time refresh are externally visible for use beyond their own file, while remaining helpers in these fragments are file-local.
Earlier absolute deadline implies higher urgency across ready-queue ordering, next-entity choice, pushable scan order, and preemption tests against the incumbent donor.

Transfer eligibility requires queued presence without current CPU residence plus affinity coverage for the destination; the running task leaves pushable tracking upon selection and may rejoin upon release when still queued and migratable.

Server scheduling requires server identity with inactive state, nonzero runtime allowance and attached bandwidth; idle-defer and missing throttle or runtime conditions suppress enqueue or replenishment.
Queue-local bandwidth is always recorded on attach, whereas global admission and overflow refusal apply only while the CPU is active; attach is idempotent and swap performs detach before attach.
Deadline high-resolution tick support has active and inert build variants, enabled only with CPU activity, high-resolution timer capability and the corresponding scheduler feature.
Yield marks the donor as yielded and refreshes clocks and consumption so throttling follows; current execution accounting applies only to deadline donors present on the deadline queue.

Wakeup prefers locality for earlier deadlines when the incumbent cannot move or is preemptible, otherwise redirects to another queue where the task remains earliest, with capacity suitability also considered when asymmetric capacity handling is active; equal deadlines use migratability and remote suitability to decide on rescheduling.

Pairwise runqueue acquisition prefers shared-lock short-circuit and try acquisition, otherwise respects a global queue order with nested acquisition, releasing the held queue when order would invert and reporting whether a release occurred.

Push, pull and balance work may temporarily release queue locks and must revalidate afterward; bandwidth, inactivity and migration paths hold the relevant queue or task-queue lock while refreshing clocks and adjusting accounting.
Global bandwidth admission is serialized by the bandwidth control lock during attach and swap, with server start attempted afterward outside that guard only when the CPU is online.

Observed runqueue state comprises current and donor tasks, stop task, deadline subqueue, domain overload tracking, CPU identity with online state, push-busy marker and server pointer; deadline entities expose deadline, runtime allowance, bandwidth share, throttle and defer markers, non-contending state and timers.

Deadline subqueue state comprises a deadline-ordered runnable tree with cached leftmost node, a separate pushable tree, a runnable count, earliest-deadline hints and a current-entity pointer established on entry and cleared on exit.

Server expiration distinguishes inapplicable throttle or runtime state, idle-deferred stop, background-consumption postponement beyond a minimum granularity, and replenish state with preemption signalling and push attempt.

Task bandwidth expiration distinguishes server delegation, inapplicable policy or boost or unthrottled states, dormant replenish-only state, offline-migration state, and runnable replenish state with preemption signalling and push attempt.

Inactivity expiration distinguishes server versus task ownership, dead or retyped tasks requiring bandwidth withdrawal and parameter clearing, and contending versus non-contending utilization, with accounting removal only when previously marked non-contending.
Next-task resolution distinguishes empty runnable state, server-entity delegation with stop-and-retry on empty delegation and server recording on success, and direct task resolution otherwise.
Bandwidth and inactivity handlers act as timer callbacks returning a restart decision and internally acquiring the appropriate queue protection before touching clocks or queues.

Dequeue, yield, wakeup preemption, migration, balance, current-accounting, entry and exit hooks connect deadline bookkeeping with generic scheduling for clocks, statistics, load tracking and overload push or pull initiation.
Task references are retained across lock-releasing searches and released afterward; timer-path release may destroy the task object, forbidding further access to its members.

Queue, donor and candidate information cached before a lock release must not be reused afterward because the candidate may have migrated or the donor changed; equality of candidate and running task is treated as unexpected.
Minimum defer-timer forwarding granularity is one millisecond.
